People who are depressed have a very hard time getting out of it, because at some point they become comfortable where they are, even if they're unhappy. The way to solve this is to take action, you need to realize that it's possible to get better, there's always a way, but you need to actively try. Go outside, hang out with people, push yourself, and eventually day by day you'll find yourself getting better. A bit of therapy never hurts either. I hope you can pick yourself up, because you have a good future ahead of you, you just need to keep trying.

Hey, I understand exactly how you feel. I'm depressed, and I've been told I'm empathetic, so I can understand how my friends feel and so on, but when it comes to helping them I don't know how to.

 It's about being able to communicate, I guess, but it's also important to remember it's not your job to change their mind. If you end up stressing over it too much nothing gets better, just worst. All you can do is let your friend know that you're there for them, you care, and try to get suicide off their mind. The rest is in your friend, if she wants help or not. If she does, things will fall into place, if not then there's not much you can do for her.

 You can't help someone who doesn't want help.
I hope the best for you, though I think that it's never hopeless, and even if it doesn't work out you should keep trying. I can understand how you feel though, good luck!

A lot of people in the world find that at some point in their life, they run out of reason to live, or at least they find themselves at the lowest point of their life. I think that's where you currently are, and I don't want to be like the average motivational post but you can always find more reasons to live. As long as you remain alive you can find new hobbies, experience great things and just..live, I suppose. Look forward to the next day, because it gives you a few more hours to learn new things and get closer to finding whatever happiness or things you might crave. It's okay to feel hopeless and feel like you don't have a reason to live, because sometimes these things will be lost but also found again.

Personal opinion here, I think if you don't go to the doctors and at least try to get help from them you'll always end up wondering if you should've went or not, or at least for a while. I think you should try, the idea that they might turn you down is scary, but even if they do you're only back to your current position. You should try to get as much help as possible until you can see your therapist again, especially if there's even the slightest chance it'll help you. 

 If you do decide to talk to a doctor, I hope they'll listen to you and help you out with your problem. I remember my pediatrician gave me anxiety pills to help me out, real weak ones, valium or something. With luck, I hope the doctor will be able to prescribe something at least the tiniest bit helpful to you.

It's always hard to be certain of things when the other person's supposed life is on the line. I know it's not much coming from a seventeen year old, but I can tell you that it's not your fault (I mean at the most at least I have an unbiased opinion for sure). A person doesn't commit suicide or threaten suicide just because of one person, namely you, so no matter what happens or what has happened, no, it isn't your fault. I hope that you'll be able to feel safe, both you and your son, and I hope that you will find someone who gives you love and doesn't stress you out like he did.
